newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide deeper in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide deeper in late trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended their earlier losses amid slow dealing late Monday afternoon in what dealers said was a delayed reaction to sharp declines on Wall Street Friday.
"The market has taken till just now to react to Friday's plunge on Wall Street. Still, the fact it is sliding on thin volume shows investors are not bailing out," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 77.15 points, or 1.56 percent, at 4,879.46. Trading volume was much lighter than average at 37.1 million shares..

The Dow Jones Industrial Average had dropped more than 247 points on Friday, its second-largest decline ever in terms of points. Late Monday, the blue-chip average was off 17.65 points at 7,677.01, having recovered from its session low.
The IPC had also improved from its day's low point of 4,863.40 points.
Traders said dealing in Mexico was slow amid caution ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, in which central bank policy-makers would review interest rates.
"It may be absurd the FOMC is still affecting the market, as no one expects rates to change, but it is and it's impacting the market," another dealer said.
News of stronger-than-expected growth by the Mexican economy in the second quarter did little to halt the slide in share prices, dealers said.
The Finance Ministry announced shortly before the opening that Mexican GDP grew 8.8 percent in the second quarter, compared with an average estimate of 5.92 percent growth in a Reuters survey MEX22.
Telefonos de Mexico led the market lower, traders said, shedding 8 centavos to 19.74 pesos.
On the broad market, decliners outpaced gainers by 72 to 18, out of 109 stocks traded.
